note: Gameplay tuning — building catalog for City View slots. Costs align with logistics_tuning development bases.
demolish_note: Salvage only (timber, nails, brick sold off), not a refund.

buildings.name: Farm
buildings.description: Fields and barns that feed the magazine and steady the muster.

buildings.name: Workshop
buildings.campaign_effect: Faster cartridge craft; +1 musket/month per level
buildings.description: A flintlock shop that turns powder, lead and paper into cartridges.

buildings.name: Depot
buildings.campaign_effect: Shorter shipment transit into this town; +8 gold/month trade per level
buildings.description: Storehouse and wagons for powder, provisions and arms.

buildings.name: Fort
buildings.campaign_effect: Lets the town enlist provincial regulars
buildings.battle_effect: Defender holds a post at start; +3 morale/+2 readiness per level; extra cover
buildings.description: Earthworks and palisades that stiffen the defense.

buildings.name: Meeting House
buildings.description: The parish meeting house that steadies local Support.

buildings.name: Militia Muster
buildings.campaign_effect: Lets the town raise militia companies
buildings.description: Drill ground where minutemen form and march to the posts.

recruit_note: GAME INVENTION. One company musters per town at a time; men come from the town's monthly manpower (base below at Support 50, scaled by Support 25-100). Militia and riflemen bring their own firelocks; regulars are armed from the town magazine. 'faction' limits who may raise a company (empty = anyone); 'requires_chapter' holds it back until that campaign chapter (continental = Congress adopts the army, 14 June 1775, the day it voted the first rifle companies). 'role' is the battlefield summary shown to the player; the battle values themselves live in the Unreal class kits.
economy_note: GAME INVENTION. Settled on the 1st of each month: levies, depot trade and workshop muskets in; army pay, building upkeep and loan interest out. A shortfall is borrowed up to credit_per_town x towns held; past that the army goes unpaid.
enemy_economy_note: GAME INVENTION. The other side settles the same accounts from its own war chest (starts at 60, never shown). A side that controls the harbour and holds its headquarters town also lands sea_subsidy_gold and sea_provisions each month. It cannot borrow: unpaid means -unpaid_morale. With gold above enemy_reserve_gold it raises its cheapest available company once a month.

recruits.name: Militia company
recruits.role: Skirmishers. Shoot best from walls and fences; unsteady in the open; no bayonets.
recruits.description: Townsmen who turn out with their own firelocks.

recruits.name: Provincial regulars
recruits.role: Line infantry. Stand in ranks and fire volleys; steadier than militia; a few bayonets.
recruits.description: Enlisted men drilled in the works and armed from the magazine.

recruits.name: Rifle company
recruits.role: Marksmen. Long rifles hit at twice a musket's range but load slowly; no bayonet, weak hand to hand.
recruits.description: Frontier riflemen with their own long rifles, voted by Congress on 14 June 1775.

recruits.name: Company officer
recruits.role: Leader. Men within 15 m of him aim steadier and load faster. Carries a light fusil.
recruits.description: A captain or lieutenant to steady the men and order their fire.

recruits.name: Company of foot
recruits.role: Line infantry. Crisp volleys in the open and the bayonet to follow.
recruits.description: A battalion company of a regiment of foot.

recruits.name: Grenadier company
recruits.role: Shock troops. The tallest, strongest men: hardest to kill and deadliest with the bayonet.
recruits.description: The regiment's right-flank company, picked for size and steadiness.

recruits.name: Light infantry company
recruits.role: Skirmishers. Fast in loose order, use cover, fire at will; lighter in a bayonet fight.
recruits.description: The regiment's left-flank company, picked for agility and marksmanship.

recruits.name: Troop of light horse
recruits.role: Dragoons (GAME INVENTION for 1775). Ride to the fight, dismount out of musket range and fight on foot with carbines; remount to move. No bayonet.
recruits.description: Farmers' sons on their own horses, mounted from the town's farms and armed from the magazine.

recruits.name: Troop of light dragoons
recruits.role: Dragoons (GAME INVENTION for 1775). Ride to the fight, dismount out of musket range and fight on foot with carbines; remount to move. No bayonet.
recruits.description: A troop of light dragoons with their carbines, pistols and sabres.
